authority: Severity reflects what a failure actually costs. HARD_FAIL blocks the release. STRONG_WARNING and SOFT_WARNING report and do not block. Unclassified checks default to STRONG_WARNING so an unreviewed check cannot silently gate a release.

severity_definitions.HARD_FAIL: Blocks the release. Money, secrets, legal exposure, or structural integrity of published pages.
severity_definitions.STRONG_WARNING: Reported prominently, does not block. Quality and hygiene.

validators.reason: five published Kindle EPUBs print these five paths on their last page. The link is baked into files that are already built, so a broken path here cannot be fixed by editing this repo - the remedy is re-uploading five books. Nothing else in the gate ties an app route to an external published artifact, and route_ownership.json alone cannot fail when both the route and its expectation are deleted together, which is why the five paths are hardcoded in the validator.
authority contracts govern what may publish
an entry that fails isComplete() is a 404 the moment it is written; 45 of them accumulated over 28 days with every other validator passing
validators.repair_evidence: proved on 2026-08-28: deleting faqs from a frozen guide fails this validator with UNRENDERABLE_ENTRY, and restore_authority_content.mjs rewrites the entry from its frozen blob and the validator passes again

validators.reason: Five published Kindle EPUBs print https://weddingpdfchecklist.com/amazon/<slug> on their last page. That hostname transposes the canonical one and is baked into files already on sale, so a host-level failure - no DNS, an invalid certificate, or the redirect losing the path - cannot be fixed by editing this repo and breaks every reader arriving from a book. validate:amazon-paths covers the five paths on the canonical host and cannot see the host the books actually print. This gate fetches all five over HTTPS on the book domain, requires a 301 to the same path on weddingchecklistpdf.com ending in a 200, and separately asserts the alias is never declared as a canonical host - a second host that renders would be a duplicate indexable copy of the whole site. It uses the canonical host as a network control so an offline machine reports UNPROVEN rather than a false red.
validators.repair_evidence: proved on 2026-08-29: the gate exited 1 with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND on all five printed URLs before weddingpdfchecklist.com was attached to the Worker, and passed once attach-book-domain.mjs created the custom domain and the deployed middleware answered 301 -> 200 on each path

validators.reason: data/cadence/policy.json restates two numbers derived from a measured rate; nothing re-derived or asserted them, and a simulated clock on 2026-08-29 showed the stored 11/5 becoming 7/3 by 2026-09-20 while the publisher kept releasing 5 a week
validators.repair_rationale: derive_capacity.mjs --check fails only when data/cadence/policy.json claims more capacity than measured throughput supports, or when new_pages_per_week no longer follows from refresh_capacity_per_week; --write is the same script re-deriving both from the same measurement, so it fixes exactly the defect the check detects.
validators.repair_evidence: proved on 2026-08-29 under a simulated clock of 2026-09-20: --check exited 1 naming refresh_capacity_per_week 11 against a measured 7.68/week, --write rewrote the policy to 7/3, and --check then exited 0

the post-payment path is reached by file path, not by import, so nothing else in the gate can see it disappear: on 2026-08-29 deleting app/api/stripe-webhook/route.ts and app/api/download/[token]/route.ts left typecheck, 54 unit tests, validate:structural and validate:registry (passed=21, hard_failed=0) all green

a URL in the sitemap with no inbound internal link is a published page the site itself does not admit exists: it can neither receive nor pass authority, and no other gate can see it because the sitemap producer (data/seo/route_ownership.json) and the link producers (the templates) were never connected. Ahrefs found six on 2026-09-03 - the five /amazon/ book pages added 2026-08-29 and /what-to-do-6-months-before-the-wedding added 2026-09-02. This gate boots the real build, reads each host's real sitemap, and reads the anchors out of the HTML the server returned, so it asserts behaviour rather than the model. Requires a build: it hard-fails rather than skipping when .next is absent, so it can never exit 0 having crawled nothing.

repair_contract: A validator may declare repair_command only when that command fixes the same defect this validator detects. scripts/selfheal/heal_until_clean.mjs runs it on failure and re-validates. Pairing a repair with a validator it does not actually fix would turn the self-heal loop into a way of making failures disappear, so an unpaired validator is the correct and honest default.
